subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw expose configurable outbound local media roots for Telegram/media sends, and if so should the canonical surface be broad `tools.fs.roots` or a narrower channel/media-specific config key?
rationale: Both paths can solve the reported message loss, but they define different public security boundaries and upgrade expectations for host-local file reads.

options.title: Choose a Canonical Root Policy
options.body: Decide between broad filesystem roots and a narrower media/channel root surface before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Telegram-Only Escape Hatch
options.body: Add a Telegram-specific media-root setting with docs and security tests, accepting a narrower but potentially duplicated policy surface.

options.title: Defer Config Expansion
options.body: Keep only managed roots and document the workaround until broader filesystem-root policy is ready.

recommendation.title: Choose a Canonical Root Policy
recommendation.body: Decide between broad filesystem roots and a narrower media/channel root surface before accepting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent media-root and fs-policy commits are closest to the affected policy boundary.
